players.product: DDR5 RCD / MRDIMM register & power chipsets, SOCAMM2, memory-interface silicon IP

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Sumeet Gagneja (his first call as Rambus CFO): Q2 revenue $207.4 million was up 15% sequentially (product revenue up 13% sequentially); CEO: 'the first time we have exceeded $200 million in revenue'. Total non-GAAP operating costs including cost of goods sold $113.7 million; operating expenses $73.5 million, up sequentially on higher SG&A; interest and other income $6.8 million; non-GAAP net income $84.4 million at an assumed 16% tax rate; non-GAAP EPS $0.77, up 24% year-over-year and 21% sequentially. Operating cash flow $61 million, capital expenditures $12 million, free cash flow $49 million. On product margin: 'Recently, as you know, we've been operating in the 60%-63% gross margin, our long-term model of 60%-65% remains intact.' Reporting change: Rambus stops presenting licensing billings and will focus its results and guidance on an ASC 606 revenue basis, as the difference to royalties revenue 'is now minimal'.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue +15% QoQ; non-GAAP EPS $0.77 (+24% YoY, +21% QoQ); FCF $49M; gross margin recently 60%-63%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Q3 2026 guidance detail: product revenue of $110 million-$116 million is 'a sequential increase of 14% at the midpoint of guidance'; contract and other revenue $25 million-$31 million; non-GAAP total operating costs including cost of sales 'between $119 million and $115 million' (as stated); capital expenditures about $13 million; non-GAAP operating profit $91 million-$101 million; $7 million of interest income; 16% tax rate and 110 million diluted shares. CEO Luc Seraphin: 'we expect another quarter of double-digit growth in Q3' in product revenue; 'Our guide for Q3 shows another 20% growth year-over-year'; 'We believe our second half is going to be stronger than our first half', but Rambus keeps guiding one quarter at a time because of platform-ramp timing and supply tightness. The first quarter, 'despite the manufacturing issue we had', was 15% higher than a year earlier.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 product revenue +14% QoQ at midpoint; contract and other $25M-$31M; non-GAAP operating profit $91M-$101M; capex about $13M

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Luc Seraphin on supply: 'No, we didn't have any capacity issue in the second quarter. We continue to see tightness in the supply chain. We continue to see lead times increasing'; with strong supplier relationships, 'at this point in time, we are able to serve the market demand'. He sees 'the tightness of the supply chain' as 'the challenge next year for the industry, not only for us', and Rambus is working with its suppliers 'to address that as early as we can'.

CEO Luc Seraphin on new module architectures: Rambus has complete chipsets for MRDIMM and LPDDR5X SOCAMM2 and remains 'on track to intercept the market as these architectures gain adoption'. 'I wouldn't say that the industry is shifting to LPDDR. I think LPDDR is actually an incremental opportunity for servers': DDR will remain dominant where server-grade scale, capacity, reliability and serviceability are required, LPDDR and SOCAMM where power efficiency matters ('We see this as complementary'). SOCAMM2 'gives us a seat at the table'; its short-run revenue outlook is modest, 'but the strategic importance is really high for us'. MRDIMM: Rambus continues to ship to customers for early system buildups and 'will not overcall the adoption curve' before the platforms ramp; for GPU head nodes, MRDIMM-type solutions 'close to the GPU's HBM' could be an option.

contracts.signal: CEO Luc Seraphin, asked whether Rambus is involved with CXMT: 'Every company that builds memory has to have a license agreement with us, and they're one of them.' He expects CXMT's success to be 'a good thing for us in the long run as well'.
